summary: Sangeeta Abhay Patil works in Indology and other fields. She earned an MD from Savitribai Phule Pune University (2005–2007) and served as an Academic Consultant at Yashwantrao Chavan Maharashtra Open University in 2023.

Sangharakshita (1925–2018) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Dhardo Rinpoche, Chien Ming Chen, and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

Sangye Tenzin (1904–1978) was a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who served as Abbot of Menri Monastery. He is also attested in 2026 as a doctoral student at the University of Virginia.

Sangyeob Cha specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from Dongguk University (2001–2008), served as HK Professor at Geumgang University (2011–2022), and worked as a researcher at Kyungpook National University in 2020.

Sanit Sinak is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned degrees from Mahamakut Buddhist University, Ramkhamhaeng University, and Silpakorn University, and served as an instructor at Mahamakut Buddhist University in 2014.

Sanjay Shakya is an assistant professor at Lumbini Buddhist University (2024) working in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his master's degree at Tribhuvan University between 2008 and 2009.

Sanjay Subrahmanyam is an historian educated at Delhi School of Economics and University of Delhi. He has held chairs and professorships at Oxford (1993–1995, 2002), EHESS (1995–2002), Collège de France (2013–2021), and UCLA (from 2005).
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under M. K. Ganguli (attested 1994) and traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. She held positions at Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, Jadavpur, Utrecht (~1968–1986), and the University of Oxford (~1991).

Sanjukta Poddar specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her MA and PhD at the University of Chicago (2015–2022), where she was a postdoctoral teaching fellow (2022), and became an assistant professor at Leiden University in 2023.
Sanne Dokter-Mersch works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi, and served there as a postdoc in 2022.

Santanu Sarkar works in Indology and related fields. Educated at North Bengal, Panchanan Barma, Burdwan, and IIT Kharagpur, he served as a PhD research scholar at IIT Kharagpur (2020–2026) and assistant professor at the University of Engineering & Management (2026).

Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Narada. He taught at the University of Rangoon, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs (2002).

Sara Frumento works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied for a DPhil in Area Studies at Wolfson College, University of Oxford (attested 2026), and has held a post at the University of Oxford.

Sara Grant (1922–2002) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. She studied at Oxford and the University of Mumbai under Richard De Smet, and taught at Sophia College (~1957–1972), Jnana-Deepa Vidyapeeth, and Christa Prema Seva Ashram (~1972–2000).

Sara L. McClintock is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Columbia, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD 2002) under Tom Tillemans, she has held posts at Lausanne, the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2003), and Emory University (attested 2026).
Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto (completed 2016) under the supervision of Jenny Purtle.

Sarah Cymbal is a scholar of history, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from SPbGUK (2017–2023) and the Russian-Armenian University (2024–2026). She serves as Director and Researcher at the Centre for the study of Silk Road art and Buddhism.

Sarah E. Fraser is a scholar in history, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, she held posts as Associate Professor at Northwestern University (1996) and Directrice d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2000).
